There are a handful of medical reasons why I think someone could be legitimately fat, including but not limited to extensive physical disability (not due to being a lard-ass, but like having lost limbs to an IED in war, or permanent nerve damage from polio, etc.) Mental health problems are not a reason.

That's not to say we shouldn't be sympathetic to those with mental health problems, including depression, but that doesn't count as a 'reason' for being fat. Hell, even most 'legitimate' reasons for being fat are irrelevant assuming you follow a proper calorie regimen. It bothers me when people take one situation out of their control (illness) and use it as an excuse for another problem they do have control over (eating too much food and exercising too little).

There are far greater problems that people face, and overcome, than depression or other irrelevant medical problems that are used as an excuse to have a cottage cheese ass.

I'm depressed and don't feel like working out, so I have CHOSEN to be fucking lazy and not do it.

I'm depressed and don't want to go for a walk outside, so I have CHOSEN to sit in front of my computer all day ( everyday? ) .

I'm clinically depressed and not fat. I did initially gain weight at the height of my breakdown last year, but only 10lbs, not 50. I actually lost it and more when I was diagnosed because my therapist suggested exercise as a part of my treatment. In addition to losing weight, I have gained more muscle than I've ever had before and grown a new appreciation for the amazing things my body can do. It's honestly done wonders for my mental health and has been an integral part of becoming a functioning human for me.

Yeah, motivation to do anything besides lay in bed has been hard for me. I'm fucking depressed, and get anxiety just thinking about leaving the house. I've been on some sort of antidepressant (or multiple) for more than half my life. My psychiatrist has told me that I will probably always need to take something. My brain just doesn't produce enough serotonin. He suspects it's genetic; my grandmother is the same as me, in that she needs to be medicated constantly as well.

I get pissed off when hams use depression or medication as an excuse to be a lazy sack of shit. Like I said, I've been on medication for more than half my life, and I've never weighed more than 145lbs (I'm 5'7"). The medication excuse is bullshit. The medications don't make you gain weight, over eating does.
